snippet.title: The Science of Protein and Its Role in Longevity, Cancer, Aging, and Building Muscle
snippet.description:
Protein is far more than a building block for muscle—it’s essential for metabolic health, insulin sensitivity, and preventing conditions like type 2 diabetes and sarcopenia. But how much do we truly need? And could too much protein, especially from meat, actually be harmful? This episode challenges the conventional RDA of 0.8 g/kg, presenting research that supports higher intakes of 1.2–2 g/kg for maintaining muscle, improving body composition, and promoting longevity. We also confront myths around protein timing and the so-called "anabolic window.” Lastly, we address concerns about protein’s links to cancer, heart disease, and kidney function, showing how exercise can redirect growth factors like IGF-1 to promote repair while mitigating risks. 

Download my “How to Train According to the Experts” guide—your go-to resource for distilled advice on training, nutrition, and supplementation from nearly 100 episodes of this show:

Most men don’t walk into clinic saying “I have ED.”

It usually starts much earlier than that.

The first layer?
Low libido.
Low psychological drive.
“I just don’t really want to.”

And once that shows up, the next phase often follows:
• weaker erections
• difficulty maintaining
• performance not what it used to be

Here’s what men need to understand:
That’s not just a bedroom issue.

Low testosterone can absolutely reduce drive — but erectile changes are also a circulation issue. They reflect endothelial function. And endothelial dysfunction is often one of the earliest warning signs of cardiovascular disease.

The penis is a vascular organ.
If blood flow is compromised there, it may be compromised elsewhere.

Sexual health is cardiovascular health.

snippet.title: OBGYN's still say this  #podcast #interview
snippet.description:
This is one of the most frustrating things I still hear in clinic:
“You’re too young for hormone therapy.”

A 42-year-old woman goes to her OB-GYN, explains she has low energy, low drive, and feels off… and the response is dismissal instead of investigation.

Here’s the truth: hormone decline doesn’t follow a birthday schedule. It’s not like you hit 43 and suddenly fall off a cliff. Some women start struggling in their early 30s. Others feel great into their 50s.

That’s why the right approach isn’t guessing — it’s testing.

When symptoms show up, you should be looking at:
• estrogen + progesterone balance
• testosterone levels (yes, women need testosterone too)
• thyroid function
• cortisol and stress physiology
• metabolic health + inflammation

Unfortunately, most conventional training barely touches hormone optimization. Even many endocrinologists aren’t trained to treat this correctly.

If you’re feeling off, don’t accept dismissal.
Get the labs. Get answers.

In this Huberman Lab Essentials episode, I explain how the body senses and uses sugar, and why understanding those mechanisms can help reduce sugar cravings. I discuss different types of sugar and how they are processed by pathways in the gut and the brain to shape appetite and the desire for specific foods. I also share many science-based tools to help curb sugar cravings and support healthy blood sugar regulation.
